lines.text: A tiny country that grew from a single castle rock to give Europe emperors, a founding father and a court. This is the story of Luxembourg.
It begins with Siegfried, a count born in the early tenth century, who would buy a rocky outcrop above the river.
In 963 he acquired that castle rock, and around it grew Luxembourg.
Far away in France, the house of Bourbon was rising. Centuries later its heirs would be the grand dukes of Luxembourg.
Meanwhile the counts of Luxembourg climbed high. Henry the Seventh became Holy Roman Emperor in 1312.
His grandson Charles the Fourth would rule the empire from Prague, one of four emperors from this small land.
For centuries the great fortress passed between Burgundy, Spain, France and Austria, until in 1867 a treaty made Luxembourg neutral and pulled its walls down.
In 1886 Robert Schuman was born in Luxembourg City, the statesman who would help found the European Union.
But neutrality did not protect it. In 1940 Nazi Germany occupied Luxembourg, for the second time in a generation.
In 1944 Luxembourg joined Belgium and the Netherlands in Benelux, a first step toward a united Europe.
In 1952 the European Court of Justice was set up, with its seat in Luxembourg.
In 1954 Jean-Claude Juncker was born, who would be prime minister for eighteen years and then lead the European Commission.
In 1981 Guillaume was born, the heir who became grand duke in 2025.
And in 2000 RTL Group took shape, a broadcasting giant grown from the old Radio Luxembourg.
From one castle rock to the heart of Europe, Luxembourg proves that small can be mighty.
